speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy with feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. To help me understand what is wrong, can you describe what your stool looks like and if you have been passing gas or having bowel movements recently?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to determine the specific type of bowel obstruction. Have you noticed if your baby has passed any meconium within the first 48 hours of birth, or is there any history of bilious (green) vomiting? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray

text: RESULTS: Dilated bowel segments with absence of gas in the rectum, suggesting a possible obstruction

text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Patient
text: The abdomen still looks swollen and the baby seems uncomfortable, especially in the lower abdomen. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: The abdominal X-ray will help us confirm if there is a blockage. Given the severe tenderness and lack of mention of early meconium passage, we must rule out Hirschsprung's disease and meconium ileus urgently. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung's disease
